ToolResultBlock(tool_use_id='toolu_bdrk_018AZ9qZUnFMeDAXEbRvjgaj', content='1	# Tomcat Tribes EncryptInterceptor Bypass Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-34486)
2	
3	[中文版本(Chinese version)](README.zh-cn.md)
4	
5	Apache Tomcat is a widely used open-source implementation of the Java Servlet, JavaServer Pages, Java Expression Language, and WebSocket technologies.
6	
7	Tomcat Tribes is the clustering framework shipped with Tomcat. Tomcat instances with Tribes enabled exchange messages with each other through Java serialization, and when an `EncryptInterceptor` is configured these serialized byte streams are transmitted in encrypted form. Under normal circumstances, a receiving Tomcat instance only deserializes a message after it has been decrypted successfully. However, during the official fix for CVE-2026-29146 (the Tribes EncryptInterceptor Padding Oracle vulnerability), a bug was introduced that fails to abort the processing pipeline when decryption fails — the raw byte stream is forwarded to downstream handlers regardless of whether decryption succeeded, and ultimately gets deserialized and executed. An attacker with network access to the Tribes receiver port (default 4000) can therefore send an unencrypted message carrying a Java deserialization payload, completely bypassing the EncryptInterceptor's encryption protection and achieving remote code execution. This vulnerability affects Apache Tomcat versions 9.0.116, 10.1.53, and 11.0.20.
8	
9	A Tomcat instance is only exploitable when all of the following conditions are met:
10	
11	- `<Cluster>` is explicitly enabled in `server.xml`
12	- An `EncryptInterceptor` is configured on the Cluster's Channel (Tribes without this interceptor already accepts unencrypted messages directly, which falls outside the scope of this CVE)
13	- The Tribes receiver port is reachable by the attacker over the network (listening on port 4000 by default)
14	- A usable deserialization gadget chain (such as Apache Commons Collections) is available on the classpath
15	
16	References:
17	
18	- <https://www.cyberkendra.com/2026/04/apache-tomcats-security-fix-opened-door.html>
19	- <https://www.herodevs.com/vulnerability-directory/cve-2026-34486>
20	- <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-69r9-qgr7-g2wj>
21	
22	## Environment Setup
23	
24	Execute the following command to start a vulnerable Tomcat 9.0.116 server with Tribes clustering and EncryptInterceptor enabled:
25	
26	```
27	docker compose up -d
28	```
29	
30	After the server starts, you can access the Tomcat default page at `http://your-ip:8080`. The Tribes receiver is listening on port 4000.
31	
32	## Vulnerability Reproduction
33	
34	The exploit leverages the EncryptInterceptor bypass to send an unencrypted Java deserialization payload to the Tribes receiver port. Since the vulnerable container ships with `commons-collections 3.2.1` on the classpath, any Apache Commons Collections gadget chain can be used to execute arbitrary system commands.
35	
36	First, generate a serialized payload using [ysoserial](https://github.com/frohoff/ysoserial) (or any equivalent tool):
37	
38	```
39	java -jar ysoserial.jar CommonsCollections6 "touch /tmp/success" > payload.ser
40	```
41	
42	Then use the provided `poc.py` script to wrap the payload in a Tribes frame and send it to the receiver port:
43	
44	```
45	python3 poc.py -t your-ip -p 4000 -f payload.ser
46	```
47	
48	![](1.png)
49	
50	Then, verify the command was executed by checking for the file inside the container:
51	
52	```
53	docker compose exec tomcat ls -la /tmp/success
54	```
55	
56	![](2.png)
57	
58	The file `/tmp/success` exists, confirming that the deserialization payload was processed and the command was executed successfully. The only trace in the Tomcat logs is a single `SEVERE: Failed to decrypt message` line, as the EncryptInterceptor logged the decryption failure but still forwarded the unencrypted payload.
59

20	    p.write(struct.pack(">I", 0))
